7 companies · run 18 Nov 2026 · spot gold $3,751, silver $44.99, copper $5.63, uranium $92.00 · 4 green, 3 blue, 0 red · grades A 3 · B 3 · n/m 1

How the values are worked out

Value vs price. Value comes from the latest reported numbers only (no targets, no forecasts) and is compared with today's price: owner earnings at today's metal prices × 12 / 15 / 25 + net cash for producers and royalties, NAV for developers and physical holders, and for growth companies the yearly growth the price needs (5 years, 15x exit, 10% US / 12% India). Profit vs price. Growth in profit and in the share price over about three years; the grade says whether the P/E fell (A ≤ −25%, B ≤ 0) or rose (C ≤ +33%, D above). Click a ticker for the full working; click a column to sort.

Screen – 2 shortlisted, 2 near misses of 7

Value that survives a lower metal price. A miner's profit follows its metal, so the P/E and growth screen is translated: shortlist = price at or below fair value (15x owner earnings at today's spot; 13x cash flow for oil), still at or below it with the metal 20% lower, volume growth of at least 5% a year (revenue growth over about 3 years with the metal-price change taken out – approximate: revenue is in the company's currency and acquisitions count as growth), and at least 10% a year over a 5-year hold with earnings flat at today's spot, sold at fair value. Guards: positive owner earnings, AISC ≤ 60% of spot where known, current results. Near miss: fair value met and one other check short. Developers and physical holders: their NAV rules (shortlist at the buy level, near miss up to 1.0× NAV). Share dilution is not checked yet.

Rules. Tier A: start at or below the 15x value, add at or below 12x. Tiers B and C: buy only with a 20% margin at 12x and AISC ≤ 60% of spot, or ≤ 0.8× NAV (0.85× physical). Red = ≥ 25x, ≥ 1.5× NAV or no valid value. Before buying: price vs 200-day average (below = buy in thirds), RSI/MACD; sell puts at 12x. [Flags]: STALE = results > ~100 days old and newer ones out (or due); price age. (Previous run.)

Profit growth vs price growth

At a glance: A 3 · B 3 · n/m 1. Profits outran the price and cheap on value (A/B + green): KGC, ERO.TO, OGC, 2899.HK.

How to read it. Growth is a yearly rate over about three years: for Indian companies Screener.in's compounded figures (net profit, latest three financial years; share price over three years); for the rest, Yahoo Finance statements from the financial year about three years back to the latest twelve months (diluted EPS, so buybacks and new shares count). P/E change = ((1 + price growth) ÷ (1 + profit growth)) ^ years − 1: negative means the share is cheaper relative to profits than at the start. Grade: A = P/E fell 25% or more · B = fell up to 25% · C = rose up to a third · D = rose more than a third · n/m = not comparable. Prices are in the exchange's currency; sales and profits as reported (m = millions, cr = crore). Profits include one-offs – check large jumps in the filing. A rising metal price lifts miners' profits faster than their prices (most gold miners grade A now); if the metal falls, profits fall faster too.

How the value is calculated

  1. Owner earnings = adjusted net income + D&A − sustaining capex, × periods a year.
  2. No re-pricing to spot: earnings stay at the company's own realised prices.
  3. Value = owner earnings × 12 (cautious) and × 15 (fair), plus net cash per share.
  4. Rule: BUY needs a 20% margin of safety at 12x and AISC ≤ 60% of spot. 25x and above is the sell zone.
Worked example: (18,356) × 4 ÷ 26,589.7m shares in CNYm, converted to HKD = HK$3.25 a share. × 12 − HK$2.94 net debt = HK$36.09 (cautious); × 15 = HK$45.84 (fair). Price HK$25.82.

How the value is calculated

  1. Owner earnings = adjusted net income + D&A − sustaining capex, × periods a year.
  2. Re-price to today's metals: ounces / pounds sold × (spot − realised price) × (1 − royalty) × (1 − tax).
  3. Value = owner earnings × 12 (cautious) and × 15 (fair), plus net cash per share.
  4. Rule: BUY needs a 20% margin of safety at 12x and AISC ≤ 60% of spot. 25x and above is the sell zone.
Worked example: (591 + 217 − 119) × 4 ÷ 1,178.0m shares = $2.34 a share; re-priced to today's metals −0.48 → $1.86. × 12 + $1.61 net cash = $23.96 (cautious); × 15 = $29.55 (fair). Price $18.56.
